---
title: "Glossary"
---

Terms used in the course, in alphabetical order. Each entry names the modules that use it.
Clinical terms are defined in plain words for engineers; they are not clinical guidance.

Ablation
: Destroying a small area of heart tissue on purpose, for example by radiofrequency heating, to stop an arrhythmia. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Action potential
: The rise and fall of the transmembrane voltage when a heart cell is excited. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Activation wavefront
: The moving boundary between excited and resting tissue. Also called the front. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Active catheter tracking
: Locating small receiver coils at a catheter's tip from MR signals so the scanner can follow it and steer the imaging plane; reported at up to 50 updates per second. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Adversarial example
: An input changed slightly, often invisibly, so that a model gives a different output; for ECG models, a small added waveform. [m46](../modules/m46-trustworthy-ai.qmd)

AI agent
: A program in which a model, usually a large language model, chooses step by step which tool to call, reads the result and continues until a goal is met or a step limit is reached. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Air kerma
: The kinetic energy that X-rays release per unit mass of air, in gray (Gy); measured at a reference point it relates to the dose at the patient's skin. [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

Aliasing
: The folding of frequencies above half the sampling rate onto lower ones; once sampled, the two cannot be told apart. [m04](../modules/m04-recording-chain.qmd)

Analytic signal
: A complex signal whose real part is the original and whose imaginary part is its Hilbert transform; its angle gives an instantaneous phase, meaningful when the signal is narrowband. [m05](../modules/m05-time-frequency.qmd)

Anisotropy
: Direction dependence of a tissue property: heart muscle conducts faster, and has lower resistance, along its fibers than across them. [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

Arrhythmia
: An abnormal heart rhythm. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Atrial fibrillation (AF)
: A fast, irregular rhythm of the upper chambers, without organized atrial activity. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Atrium (plural atria)
: One of the two upper chambers of the heart. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Attention
: In a neural network, a weighted average of value vectors whose weights come from how well a query matches each key, normalized by a softmax. The building block of the transformer. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Audit log
: An append-only record of every step an agent took: the tool, its arguments, the policy decision and the result, so a person can check the run afterwards. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Average precision (PR AUC)
: The area under the precision–recall curve, averaged over thresholds. Unlike the ROC AUC it falls when positives are rare. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Average symmetric surface distance (ASSD)
: The mean distance between two surfaces, measured from each to the other; a typical-error measure for segmentations. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Bayesian optimization
: Choosing where to measure next by modelling an unknown function with a probabilistic surrogate, such as a Gaussian process, and maximizing an acquisition function. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Bipolar electrogram
: The difference between the signals of two nearby electrodes. It acts like a spatial derivative: it keeps local detail and rejects distant activity, but depends on the bipole's orientation to the wavefront. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

C-arm
: A fluoroscopy system with the X-ray source and detector on opposite ends of a C-shaped arm that rotates around the patient. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Cardiac sarcoidosis
: Inflammation of the heart by granulomas, which can cause conduction block and ventricular tachycardia; FDG PET can show active inflammation. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Cavotricuspid isthmus (CTI)
: The strip of right atrial tissue between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid valve; the usual ablation target for typical atrial flutter. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Central-slice theorem
: The 1-D Fourier transform of a projection equals the 2-D Fourier transform of the image along the line through the origin at the same angle; it is why projections at enough angles determine a CT slice. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Clique
: A small group of electrodes, such as a triangle or a square, whose bipoles are combined to estimate the local electric field. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Cohen's kappa
: Agreement between two raters or methods beyond what chance would give: (observed − expected agreement) / (1 − expected agreement). [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Collocation point
: A point where a governing equation is checked during fitting; it needs no measurement. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Computed tomography (CT)
: Imaging that measures X-ray attenuation along many lines through the body and reconstructs cross-sectional slices from those measurements. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Concordance index (C index)
: For a risk score, the share of comparable patient pairs in which the patient with the earlier event had the higher score; 0.5 is chance. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Condition number
: The ratio of a matrix's largest to smallest singular value; it bounds how much a relative error in the data can grow in the solution. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Conducting channel
: A corridor of surviving tissue through scar that may carry a reentrant ventricular tachycardia; post-processing software can identify candidate channels on LGE. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Conduction velocity
: The speed at which the activation wavefront travels through tissue, in m/s (1 m/s = 1 mm/ms). [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd), [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Conformal prediction
: A method that turns a model's scores into a set of possible answers that contains the true one at a chosen rate, using a held-out calibration set. [m46](../modules/m46-trustworthy-ai.qmd)

Contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR)
: The difference between two tissues' mean signals divided by the noise standard deviation; it decides whether they can be told apart, and averaging n independent samples multiplies it by the square root of n. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd), [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

Contrastive learning
: Self-supervised learning that pulls the embeddings of matched pairs, such as two recordings of one patient, together and pushes unmatched pairs apart. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Core-conductor model
: A model of a cell strand in which intracellular current flows along the strand and leaks out through the membrane; it gives membrane current as the second derivative of transmembrane voltage. [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

Cotangent Laplacian
: The standard discretization of the Laplace–Beltrami operator on a triangle mesh: each edge is weighted by half the sum of the cotangents of the two angles opposite it. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Cross-entropy
: The loss most classifiers minimize: minus the log of the probability given to the true class. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Current dipole
: A current source and an equal sink very close together; its strength is current times separation, and its potential falls as one over distance squared. [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

CUSUM
: Cumulative sum: a running sum of deviations above a target, reset at zero, that raises an alarm when it crosses a threshold. Used to detect a lasting shift in a monitored quantity. [m45](../modules/m45-ai-evidence-regulation.qmd)

Data augmentation
: Training on altered copies of the data (for example, flipped or noisier signals) so a model ignores the alteration. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Dataset shift
: Any difference between the data a model was trained on and the data where it is used: in class mix (prior shift), in the recordings (covariate shift) or in what labels mean. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

De-identification
: Removing or coarsening information in health data so that it no longer identifies a person, for example by removing direct identifiers and grouping quasi-identifiers; the rules differ by country. [m47](../modules/m47-data-deployment-engineering.qmd)

Decapolar catheter
: A catheter with ten electrodes along its shaft. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Dice coefficient
: Overlap of a predicted and a true region: twice the shared area over the sum of the two areas, from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (identical). [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd), [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Discrepancy principle
: Choosing a regularization parameter so that the model fits the data only as closely as the noise level allows. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd), [m32](../modules/m32-capstone-ecg-imaging.qmd)

Discrete Picard condition
: The requirement that the data's coefficients in the singular vectors fall faster than the singular values; without it no regularized solution is good. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Dominant frequency
: The frequency of the largest spectral peak in a search band; for electrograms it tracks the activation rate only after suitable preprocessing. [m05](../modules/m05-time-frequency.qmd), [m29](../modules/m29-complex-maps.qmd)

Double layer
: A surface covered with current dipoles pointing normal to it; a uniform double layer's potential is proportional to the solid angle it subtends. [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

ECG gating
: Using the electrocardiogram to keep only imaging data from a chosen part of the cardiac cycle, so that the moving heart appears still. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Edema (myocardial)
: Excess water in heart tissue after injury such as ablation; bright on T2-weighted MRI, it includes reversible injury and fades over time. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Eikonal equation
: The equation v |grad T| = 1 linking an activation-time map T to the local conduction speed v. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd), [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Electrogram
: The voltage an electrode records from currents crossing cell membranes nearby. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Embedding
: A vector that represents an input, such as a beat or a sentence, so that similar inputs get nearby vectors. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Endocardium
: The inner surface of the heart wall. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ensemble
: A set of models trained with different random choices; their spread is used as an uncertainty estimate. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Error budget
: A list of the error sources in a chain of steps with their sizes; independent, unbiased errors add in quadrature, and biases add directly. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Euler characteristic
: V − E + F for a mesh with V vertices, E edges and F faces; 2 for a closed surface without handles, one less for each hole cut into it. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Expected improvement
: An acquisition function: the average amount by which a new measurement is expected to beat the best value so far. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

External validation
: Testing a frozen model on data from another place or time that played no part in training or tuning. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Extracellular volume (ECV)
: The fraction of a tissue's volume outside cells. MRI estimates it from T1 before and after gadolinium and the hematocrit; scar and fibrosis raise it. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Far-field signal
: Activity that an electrode picks up from tissue that is not directly under it. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

Fast marching method
: An algorithm that solves the eikonal equation by advancing a front from the source in order of arrival, on grids or triangle meshes. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

FDG (fluorodeoxyglucose)
: A glucose analog labeled with fluorine-18; cells that use much glucose, including inflammatory cells, take it up and show on PET. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Feature attribution
: A score for how much each input feature, such as each sample of an ECG, contributed to a model's output for one input. [m46](../modules/m46-trustworthy-ai.qmd)

Federated learning
: Training one model across sites that keep their data; only model updates are shared. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Fibrosis
: Replacement of heart muscle by connective tissue. In the atria it can be estimated on late-gadolinium MRI. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Fiducial localization error (FLE)
: The error in locating a landmark used for registration, in either the image or the map. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Fiducial registration error (FRE)
: The residual distance between registered landmarks after a fit; its expected value depends on the number of landmarks and FLE, not on their layout. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Filter factor
: The weight a regularization method gives each singular component of the solution: 1 or 0 for truncated SVD, s²/(s² + λ²) for Tikhonov. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Filtered back-projection
: CT reconstruction that filters each projection with a ramp in frequency and smears it back along its lines; without the filter the image is blurred. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Fluoroscopy
: Continuous or pulsed X-ray imaging that shows a moving shadow image, used to guide catheters, sheaths and leads. [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

Focal loss
: A cross-entropy that down-weights examples the model already gets right, so training attends to rare and hard ones. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Focal source
: A small region from which activation spreads outward. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Fossa ovalis
: The thin central part of the wall between the two atria, where a needle usually crosses from the right atrium to the left. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Foundation model
: A large model pretrained on broad, mostly unlabeled data and then adapted to many downstream tasks. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Full width at half maximum (FWHM)
: The width of a blur between the two points where it falls to half its peak; for a Gaussian, about 2.355 standard deviations. Used to quote the spatial resolution of scanners. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd), [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd), [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Gadolinium contrast
: An MRI contrast agent that shortens T1 in proportion to its concentration and stays outside cells, so it accumulates where there is more extracellular space. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Gaussian mixture model
: A probability model that describes data as a weighted sum of normal distributions; fitted with the EM algorithm to find clusters without labels. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Gaussian process
: A probability model over functions; given measurements, it gives a mean estimate and an uncertainty at every other point. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Generalized cross-validation (GCV)
: Choosing a regularization parameter by minimizing a predicted-error function of the data, without a noise estimate. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Geodesic distance
: The length of the shortest path between two points that stays on a surface. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd), [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Graph convolution
: A network layer that mixes each point's features with those of its neighbors on a graph, such as the vertices of a mapping mesh. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Grating lobe
: A false, full-strength copy of an array's beam that appears when its elements are spaced more than half a wavelength apart for the steering used; echoes from it are drawn in the wrong direction. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Group delay
: How long a filter delays the envelope of a signal at a given frequency; causal filters shift features such as activation times by it. [m04](../modules/m04-recording-chain.qmd)

Guardrail
: A rule enforced outside the model that limits what an agent may do, such as a tool allowlist, a schema check or a human approval step. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Half-life
: The time for a radioactive tracer's activity to halve; 109.73 minutes for fluorine-18. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Half-value layer (HVL)
: The thickness of a material that halves the intensity of an X-ray beam; for a narrow beam of one energy it is ln 2 divided by the attenuation coefficient. [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

Hallucination
: Output of a language model that reads as fluent and confident but is false or unsupported, such as an invented number or reference. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Hausdorff distance
: The largest distance from any point of one surface to the other surface, in either direction; one stray island sets it. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Heat method
: A way to compute geodesic distance on a mesh: diffuse heat briefly from the source, normalize its gradient, then solve a Poisson equation. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Hematocrit
: The fraction of blood volume made up of red cells; gadolinium in blood is confined to the rest, the plasma. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Hounsfield unit (HU)
: The CT number scale, 1000 (μ − μ_water)/(μ_water − μ_air): water is 0 and air −1000. Values depend on the X-ray beam's energy. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Human approval step
: A point in an agent's run where a person must accept or decline an action, such as any write, before it is carried out. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Ill-posed problem
: A problem whose solution fails to exist, to be unique or to depend continuously on the data; small data errors then cause large solution errors. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Image intensity ratio (IIR)
: An LGE wall intensity divided by the mean blood-pool intensity, used to compare scans that have no absolute intensity scale; thresholds on it define atrial fibrosis or scar. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Implantable loop recorder (ILR)
: A small device placed under the skin that records the ECG for years and sends alerts when its detector fires. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Integrated gradients
: A feature-attribution method that averages the model's gradient along a straight path from a baseline input to the actual input; the attributions add up to the change in output. [m46](../modules/m46-trustworthy-ai.qmd)

Interventional MRI
: Performing a procedure, such as catheter ablation, inside an MRI scanner with real-time images instead of fluoroscopy. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Intracardiac echocardiography (ICE)
: Ultrasound imaging from a catheter inside the heart, used during procedures to see anatomy and build shells. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Intrinsic deflection
: The steepest downstroke of a unipolar electrogram, used to mark local activation. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Inverse problem
: Recovering sources from measurements, the reverse of the forward problem that predicts measurements from sources. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd), [m32](../modules/m32-capstone-ecg-imaging.qmd)

Inversion recovery
: An MRI preparation that flips the longitudinal magnetization with a 180° pulse and reads the image while it recovers; a tissue has no signal at T1 ln 2. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Iodinated contrast
: An iodine-containing agent injected into the blood; iodine attenuates X-rays strongly, so the blood pool stands out from the heart wall on CT. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Isocenter
: The point a C-arm rotates about; structures there are imaged at a fixed magnification. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Isthmus (VT)
: A narrow channel of conducting tissue, bounded by scar or anatomical barriers, that a reentrant ventricular tachycardia passes through. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Jaccard index
: Overlap of two regions as intersection over union; Dice = 2J/(1 + J). [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

k-anonymity
: A property of a released table: every record shares its quasi-identifier values with at least k − 1 others, so a match by those values points to at least k records. [m47](../modules/m47-data-deployment-engineering.qmd)

Kerma-area product (KAP)
: Air kerma times the area of the X-ray beam, in Gy·cm²; the same at any distance along the beam, so it describes the total radiation delivered. Also called dose-area product. [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

L-curve
: A log-log plot of solution size against residual size over all regularization parameters; its corner is one way to choose the parameter. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd), [m32](../modules/m32-capstone-ecg-imaging.qmd)

Laplace–Beltrami operator
: The Laplacian on a curved surface: the divergence of the surface gradient. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Large language model (LLM)
: A transformer trained on very large amounts of text to predict the next token; it can follow instructions and answer questions in text. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Larmor frequency
: The frequency at which nuclear magnetization precesses in a magnetic field: 42.58 MHz per tesla for protons, about 64 MHz at 1.5 T. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE)
: MRI taken some minutes after a gadolinium contrast injection, when scar and fibrosis appear bright. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd), [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Lead field
: An electrode's sensitivity to sources everywhere: by reciprocity, the gradient of the potential it would create by injecting unit current. [m02](../modules/m02-volume-conduction.qmd)

Leave-one-patient-out
: A test scheme that trains on all patients but one and tests on that one, in turn, so no patient is in both sets. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd)

Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO)
: A catheter procedure that closes the left atrial appendage with an implanted device. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Lesion gap
: A segment of an intended ablation line where the tissue was not destroyed, through which conduction can recover. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Lesion metabolic activity
: A PET measure of a lesion: its partial-volume-corrected mean uptake times its volume. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Levenberg–Marquardt method
: An iterative method for nonlinear least squares that blends Gauss–Newton steps with damped gradient steps. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Likelihood ratio
: How much a test result changes the odds of disease: for a positive result, sensitivity divided by one minus specificity; for a negative result, one minus sensitivity divided by specificity. Post-test odds are pre-test odds times the likelihood ratio. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd)

Linear probe
: A linear classifier trained on the frozen features of a pretrained model, used to measure how much those features already encode. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Local activation time
: The moment the activation wavefront reaches a given site. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Locally Delaunay edge
: A mesh edge whose two opposite angles add up to at most 180°; its cotangent weight is then not negative. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Low-voltage area
: A region whose bipolar voltage falls below a chosen cut-off. It is often read as scar, but the voltage also depends on the catheter and the wavefront. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
: Imaging of hydrogen nuclei in a strong magnetic field, with contrast from how their magnetization relaxes and position encoded by field gradients. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Magnetohydrodynamic voltage
: A voltage induced when conducting blood flows across a strong magnetic field; it distorts the ECG and electrograms inside an MRI scanner. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Magnification (projection)
: How much larger a structure appears on the detector than its true size: source-to-detector over source-to-object distance. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Membrane current
: Current crossing the cell membrane, positive outward; ahead of a wavefront it flows out (a source) and behind it flows in (a sink). [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

Method of images
: Solving a problem with a flat boundary by adding mirror sources that make the boundary conditions hold; for two conductors the mirror source has strength (sigma1 - sigma2)/(sigma1 + sigma2) times the original. [m02](../modules/m02-volume-conduction.qmd)

Model card
: A short document released with a trained model that states its intended use, out-of-scope uses, training and evaluation data, metrics overall and by group, and limitations. [m47](../modules/m47-data-deployment-engineering.qmd)

Myocardial infarction
: Death of an area of heart muscle caused by loss of its blood supply. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Negative predictive value (NPV)
: The share of negative results that are truly negative; like the positive predictive value, it depends on prevalence. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd), [m35](../modules/m35-machine-learning.qmd)

Net benefit
: In decision-curve analysis, true positives minus false positives weighted by the odds of the threshold probability, per patient. It compares a model with acting on everyone or no one. [m45](../modules/m45-ai-evidence-regulation.qmd)

Noncontact mapping
: Reconstructing endocardial potentials from a multielectrode probe that floats in the cavity, by solving an inverse problem. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Normalized surface Dice (NSD)
: The share of two surfaces lying within a chosen tolerance of each other. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Notch filter
: A narrow band-stop filter used to remove mains interference at 50 or 60 Hz. [m04](../modules/m04-recording-chain.qmd)

Nyquist frequency
: Half the sampling rate: the highest frequency a sampled signal can represent without aliasing. [m04](../modules/m04-recording-chain.qmd)

Omnipolar electrogram
: A signal built from a clique by estimating the local electric field and reading it along the direction of propagation, which removes most orientation dependence. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Otsu's threshold
: The intensity cut that splits a histogram into two classes with the largest between-class variance; used as a data-driven threshold for scar. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Out-of-distribution (OOD) input
: An input unlike the data a model was trained on, such as a recording from a new device or with heavy noise, for which its outputs are not reliable. [m46](../modules/m46-trustworthy-ai.qmd)

Outflow tract
: The part of a ventricle leading to its great artery (pulmonary artery on the right, aorta on the left); a common origin of idiopathic premature ventricular beats. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Pace mapping
: Pacing from a catheter at candidate sites and comparing the paced 12-lead ECG with the ECG of the arrhythmia, to find where the arrhythmia starts. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Pacing
: Stimulating the heart electrically from an electrode at a chosen site. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Partial-volume effect
: A voxel, or a region blurred by the scanner, that holds more than one tissue reads a mixture of their values, so thin or small structures lose contrast and change apparent size. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd), [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd), [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd)

Passive catheter visualization
: Seeing a catheter on real-time MR images through the signal void or artifact its materials cause; it shows one plane at a time. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Phase-sensitive inversion recovery (PSIR)
: An LGE reconstruction that keeps the sign of the recovering magnetization, so it is much less sensitive to the chosen inversion time than a magnitude image. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Phased array
: A row of transducer elements whose firing delays steer and focus the beam electronically, without moving the probe. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Photoplethysmography (PPG)
: Measuring blood-volume changes in tissue with light; the basis of pulse sensing in watches and trackers. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Physics-informed neural network (PINN)
: A neural network trained on a loss that adds the residual of a governing equation to the data misfit. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Point-spread function (PSF)
: The image an imaging system makes of a single point: the blur it applies to everything it shows. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd)

Poisson's equation
: The equation the potential obeys in a volume conductor, div(sigma grad phi) = -I_v: Ohm's law plus current conservation. [m02](../modules/m02-volume-conduction.qmd)

Positive predictive value (PPV)
: The share of positive results (alerts, flags) that are truly positive; it depends on prevalence. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd), [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd), [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd)

Positron emission tomography (PET)
: Imaging of a tracer that emits positrons; each annihilation sends two photons in opposite directions, detected together to define a line through the source. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Pre-test probability
: The probability of a condition before a test result is known, for example its prevalence in the group tested. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd)

Predetermined change control plan (PCCP)
: A plan, authorized with an AI-enabled device's marketing submission, that describes planned changes to the device and how each will be validated, so those changes need no new submission. [m45](../modules/m45-ai-evidence-regulation.qmd)

Premature beat
: A beat that comes earlier than expected, usually followed by a longer interval; a common cause of false AF alerts. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Premature ventricular contraction (PVC)
: An extra beat that starts in a ventricle earlier than the next normal beat. [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Prompt injection
: Text inside a document or tool output that tries to make a language model follow new instructions, such as a hidden request to delete files. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Pulmonary vein isolation (PVI)
: Ablation that encircles the pulmonary veins so that their electrical activity cannot reach the left atrium. [m39](../modules/m39-ai-electrograms-maps.qmd), [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Pulmonary vein reconnection
: Recovery of conduction between a pulmonary vein and the left atrium after isolation, usually through a gap in the lesion line. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Quantization (integer)
: Storing a model's weights or activations, or a signal's samples, as integers with a scale and zero point instead of floating-point numbers; it saves memory and computation at the cost of rounding error. [m47](../modules/m47-data-deployment-engineering.qmd)

Quantization noise
: The rounding error of an analog-to-digital converter, with standard deviation one step over the square root of 12. [m04](../modules/m04-recording-chain.qmd)

Quantum noise
: Image noise caused by the random arrival of photons; with Poisson counts its standard deviation is the square root of the mean, so noise falls only as the square root of dose. [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

Quasi-identifier
: A field that does not name a person on its own but can identify them in combination with others, such as age, sex, region or a procedure date. [m47](../modules/m47-data-deployment-engineering.qmd)

Quasi-static approximation
: Treating bioelectric fields as if they followed their sources instantly, neglecting capacitive, inductive and propagation effects in the volume conductor. [m02](../modules/m02-volume-conduction.qmd)

Radial basis function
: A function of the distance to a centre, such as a Gaussian; sums of them represent smooth maps. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

Radon transform
: The set of line integrals of an image over all lines in the plane, indexed by angle and offset; a CT scanner measures it. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Randomized controlled trial (RCT)
: A study that assigns participants at random to an intervention or a comparison, so that differences in outcome can be attributed to the intervention. [m45](../modules/m45-ai-evidence-regulation.qmd)

Receptive field
: The stretch of input that one output of a network depends on. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Reciprocity
: Helmholtz's result that the potential a source produces at an electrode equals the source dotted with the field the electrode would create by injecting unit current. [m02](../modules/m02-volume-conduction.qmd)

Recovery coefficient
: The fraction of a structure's true uptake (or contrast) that a blurred image measures; well below 1 for structures about as thin as the resolution. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Reference level (radiation dose)
: A benchmark for the typical dose of a procedure type, set from surveys (for example the third quartile of recorded doses); used to compare and optimize practice, not as a limit for one patient. [m49](../modules/m49-fluoroscopy-radiation.qmd)

Reference standard
: The best available method for deciding whether a condition is present, against which a test or model is judged; its own errors limit any measured accuracy. [m45](../modules/m45-ai-evidence-regulation.qmd)

Regularization
: Adding information or constraints, such as a penalty on solution size, so that an ill-posed problem gives a stable answer. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Remote monitoring
: Sending data from an implanted or wearable device to a clinic, where alerts are reviewed. [m38](../modules/m38-wearables-monitoring.qmd)

Repetition time (TR)
: The time between successive excitations in an MRI sequence; a real-time frame takes about the number of lines times TR. [m53](../modules/m53-lesion-imaging-interventional-mri.qmd)

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
: Answering with a language model after giving it passages retrieved from a chosen document collection, so that the answer can rest on, and cite, those passages. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

RR interval
: The time between two successive R peaks of the ECG, one ventricular beat to the next. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Scar
: Fibrous tissue that has replaced heart muscle. It conducts poorly or not at all. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Segmentation
: Labelling which voxels of an image belong to a structure, such as the left atrium. [m40](../modules/m40-ai-imaging-substrate.qmd)

Self-supervised learning
: Learning representations from unlabeled data with a training task built from the data themselves, such as matching two views of one recording. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT)
: Tomographic imaging of a tracer that emits single gamma photons, whose direction is set by a collimator. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Singular value decomposition (SVD)
: Writing a matrix as a sum of rank-one terms s u vᵀ with orthonormal vectors and non-negative singular values s. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Sinogram
: The Radon transform drawn as an image: one row of line integrals per projection angle. A point traces a sine curve in it. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Sinus rhythm
: The normal heartbeat, started by the heart's own pacemaker. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Softmax
: The function that turns a vector of scores into probabilities that are positive and sum to one. [m37](../modules/m37-ai-ecg.qmd)

Solid angle
: The area a surface covers on a unit sphere centered on the observer, in steradians; a full sphere is 4 pi. [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

Source and sink
: Places where current leaves cells into the extracellular space (source) or enters them from it (sink); every source has a matching sink. [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd)

Spatial frequency
: How quickly a pattern varies in space, in rad/mm. Fine detail has high spatial frequency. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Spatial resolution
: How close two structures can be and still appear separate in an image; often quoted as the FWHM of the point-spread function. [m48](../modules/m48-imaging-workflow.qmd)

Spectral leakage
: Power from one frequency spreading into others because a finite record is a windowed signal; window choice controls it. [m05](../modules/m05-time-frequency.qmd)

Speed-of-sound assumption
: Ultrasound systems convert echo time to depth with one assumed speed of sound, commonly 1540 m/s; tissue that is faster or slower is drawn shorter or longer. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Standardized uptake value (SUV)
: PET activity concentration divided by the injected activity per unit body weight, after decay correction; 1 means uniform distribution. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Surrogate model
: A fast approximation of a slow model, fitted to runs of it and valid only in the range it was trained on. [m42](../modules/m42-physics-informed-ml.qmd)

T1 (longitudinal relaxation time)
: The time constant with which magnetization along the field recovers after it is disturbed; gadolinium shortens it. [m52](../modules/m52-cardiac-mri.qmd)

Target registration error (TRE)
: The error after registration at a point not used for the fit, such as an ablation target; it grows with distance from the landmarks. [m55](../modules/m55-multimodal-capstone.qmd)

Temporal resolution
: How short a time span one image represents. In cardiac CT it is about half the gantry rotation time with one X-ray source and a quarter with two. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

Test-retest variability
: How much a measurement changes when repeated on the same subject with nothing changed; it sets the smallest change that can be trusted. [m54](../modules/m54-nuclear-imaging.qmd)

Tetralogy of Fallot
: A congenital heart defect affecting the right ventricular outflow and the ventricular septum. After surgical repair, ventricular tachycardia can use isthmuses bounded by patches and scars. [m51](../modules/m51-cardiac-ct.qmd)

TF-IDF
: Term frequency times inverse document frequency: a word weight that grows with how often the word appears in a document and with how rare it is across the collection. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Tikhonov regularization
: Least squares plus a penalty λ² times the squared size of the solution (or of its derivatives). [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd), [m32](../modules/m32-capstone-ecg-imaging.qmd)

Token
: A unit of text, often a word or part of a word, that a language model reads and writes. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Tool schema
: The declared arguments of an agent's tool, with their types, units and allowed ranges, checked before the tool runs. [m44](../modules/m44-agentic-ai.qmd)

Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)
: Ultrasound imaging of the heart from a probe in the esophagus, behind the left atrium. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Transformer
: A neural-network architecture built from attention layers; the basis of most large language models and of many ECG foundation models. [m43](../modules/m43-foundation-models-llms.qmd)

Transmembrane voltage
: The voltage across a cell membrane, inside minus outside. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Transseptal puncture
: Crossing from the right atrium to the left atrium through the interatrial septum, usually at the fossa ovalis, with a needle and sheath. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)
: Ultrasound imaging of the heart from a probe on the chest wall. [m50](../modules/m50-intracardiac-echo.qmd)

Triangle mesh
: A surface stored as vertices, edges and triangular faces; mapping systems store the chamber geometry this way. [m06](../modules/m06-meshes-geodesics.qmd)

Truncated SVD
: Regularization that keeps only the components of the largest singular values. [m07](../modules/m07-inverse-problems.qmd)

Unipolar electrogram
: The signal of one electrode measured against a distant reference electrode. It sees local and far-field activity. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ventricle
: One of the two lower chambers of the heart. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd)

Ventricular tachycardia
: A fast rhythm that starts in the ventricles. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m41](../modules/m41-ai-origin-localization.qmd)

Volume conductor
: The conducting medium (tissue and blood) through which currents spread from their sources to the electrodes. [m03](../modules/m03-electrograms.qmd), [m01](../modules/m01-bioelectric-sources.qmd), [m02](../modules/m02-volume-conduction.qmd)

Wavelet transform
: A time-frequency analysis that correlates the signal with scaled copies of a short wavelet, using short windows for high frequencies and long ones for low. [m05](../modules/m05-time-frequency.qmd)

Welch's method
: Estimating a power spectrum by averaging the spectra of several segments, which lowers the variance at the cost of resolution. [m05](../modules/m05-time-frequency.qmd)

WFDB format
: The Waveform Database format used by PhysioNet: integer samples in a signal file and a text header that gives the sampling rate, gain, baseline and units needed to convert them to physical values. [m47](../modules/m47-data-deployment-engineering.qmd)

Zero-phase filtering
: Filtering a record forward and then backward so that phase shifts cancel; it removes filter delay but needs the whole record, so it is offline only. [m04](../modules/m04-recording-chain.qmd)
